featured_reviews.name: Anmol Sanyasi
featured_reviews.review_text:
We went to Flavors at Bay near Hotel Hira mainly because it was convenient for us. Unfortunately, the food was a big disappointment.

I understand that it’s a vegetarian restaurant and spices are an important part of Indian cooking, but spices should complement the meal — not completely overpower it. Everything we ordered tasted like it was just packed with masala and nothing else.

We ordered momos, and they were honestly the worst part of the meal. They didn’t taste like real momos at all. Instead of a proper filling, it felt like a dough ball stuffed with pure spices. The taste matched how it looked — just overwhelming masala with no balance. Coming from a Nepali background where we eat momos often, this was really disappointing.

The biryani was the same story. It was mostly spice with very little flavor or balance beyond that.

The service itself was good and the staff were polite. The location was convenient for us as well. However, the restaurant felt quite empty and overall the food experience was not good. Unfortunately, the heavy spices even gave us heartburn afterwards.

We really wanted to enjoy the meal, but it ended up being a very disappointing experience.

featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently had a wonderful dining experience at Flavours at Bay - Pure Veg and Jain Restaurant. The restaurant truly stands out for its pure vegetarian and Jain-friendly menu, offering a wide variety of fresh, flavorful dishes.

The ambience is clean, calm, and perfect for both family dinners and casual outings. The staff is polite, attentive, and ensures quick service without compromising on quality. Every dish we tried was well-prepared, delicious, and beautifully presented.

What I really appreciated is their commitment to Jain food preparation standards while still maintaining rich taste and variety. The desserts were also a great highlight!

Overall, a fantastic place for anyone looking for pure veg and Jain cuisine with great taste and a pleasant dining atmosphere. Highly recommended for family meals and special occasions.

featured_reviews.name: Pratik Mehta
featured_reviews.review_text:
We visited last Saturday with a group of 25 ppl for my wife's birthday. Food is fine but on salty side even after mentioning that after our appetizers.
Even though we were such a big group, we were not able to spot any servers/waiters available while making repetitive orders. Also few orders we were either delayed or not delivered on our tables. On reminding the new staff (as old staff had vanished), they punched in repeat item in our bill, even though delivery happened only once! Due to their poor service I had to pay for an extra Juice! Not a nice experience.
When we are big group, and several guests have multiple choice of food, it is difficult for us to track but I would expect the restaurant staff to be able to handle accurate billing for large group of guests.

On discussing the same with owner (Rahul Jain), he said he will look in the CCTV footage and refund my amount via UPI. On following up, he said he did not get time but will refund the amount. I shared him 2 different UPI however both time he said incorrect UPI.
Later he changes his statement that no extra payment was charged! And then again he says that visit our restaurant where he can pay me in cash.
Looking at this behaviour, i will not like to even like to recommend this place to anyone.

featured_reviews.name: Burjiz
featured_reviews.review_text:
Golden Chimney offered a comfortable and enjoyable dining experience during our visit.

The ambience inside the restaurant was quite good, especially after entering from the outside summer heat into the air-conditioned seating area.

There happened to be an IPL match playing during the visit as well, which added a lively atmosphere without making the place feel too noisy or chaotic.

For drinks, I ordered a fresh lime water, which was refreshing and suited the weather well.

For starters, we ordered the Murgh Lasoni Tikka and Classic Chicken Chilly. Both dishes were enjoyable, though the Murgh Lasoni Tikka stood out more for its flavour and preparation.

For the mains, we had the Butter Chicken, which was well prepared and satisfying.

Service was good, seating was comfortable, and overall the restaurant provided a pleasant dine-in experience.

All in all, a good restaurant option in the Opera House / Lamington Road area for a relaxed lunch or dinner with decent food and ambience.

featured_reviews.name: Anmol Sanyasi
featured_reviews.review_text:
From the very first meal, Golden Chimney completely won us over. The food is absolutely delicious — every dish is rich in flavor, beautifully balanced, and full of authentic taste. You can truly taste Mumbai in the food — the spices, the freshness, and the variety all come together perfectly. Each bite felt thoughtfully prepared and full of character.
What made our experience even more special was the staff. They are incredibly gentle, kind, and genuinely thoughtful. The hospitality here stands out. They pay attention to every detail and make sure you feel comfortable and taken care of. Whether it was helping us choose dishes or checking in to make sure everything was perfect, their service was warm and sincere. We were visiting Mumbai from outside the city for just four days, and we ended up eating at Golden Chimney four out of five days — that says everything. When you find a place that combines amazing food with outstanding hospitality, you naturally want to return. Every time we came back, the quality was consistent and impressive.
The money we spent was absolutely worth it.
The portion sizes, the flavor, the cleanliness, and the service all reflect great value for the price.
It's rare to find a restaurant where both the food and the people leave such a lasting impression.
If you're in Mumbai and want authentic, flavorful food with heartfelt hospitality, Golden Chimney is a must-visit. We will definitely return the next time we are in the city.

featured_reviews.name: Burjiz
featured_reviews.review_text:
Flute 24 Hrs had a mixed dining experience overall.

The starters were quite good and flavourful. We ordered the Korean Style Chicken and Murgh Phoolzadi Kebab, both of which were enjoyable and well prepared.

However, the mains was a disappointment. We ordered the Murg Angara, and it lacked proper flavour and tasted quite off compared to the strong start from the appetizers. I also felt the recommendation for the mains could have been better.

Something unique about Flute in comparison to most other restaurants is that a 5% service fee is included and charged to the bill. This is interesting because tipping in India is optional as far as I am aware. This resulted in a modest increase in the bill of around ₹100 for the three dishes. However I would usually tip more but because the service fee was included it made little sense to top anything and felt somewhat redundant.

The service was nice as per my expectation but this practice is one which I have encountered in few restaurants and certainly is not a norm and so is something to be aware about.

The restaurant otherwise was good though but slightly priced on the premium side.

I thought some items were inappropriately priced. One small roti at ₹88 (excluding any taxes) seemed like a rip off because it averaged 3-4 rotis on just one dish so felt a bit unusual seeing ₹300 on a side dish of a basic small roti.

That said, the ambience was quite nice. The restaurant was air-conditioned, comfortable and relaxing, with an IPL match playing alongside mild instrumental music which made for a calm dining atmosphere.

Overall, good starters and ambience, but inconsistent mains and somewhat inflated pricing.

For the mains, we had Chicken Lehsuni, Bhatti Da Murg, and Cheese Garlic Naan – the Lehsuni Chicken was undoubtedly the star of the show with its bold, garlicky taste. Mutton Rogan Josh also stood out with its rich spicy and aromatic flavour. The Chicken Biryani that followed was aromatic and satisfying.

Desserts were a highlight – the Butterscotch Ice Cream, Malai Kulfi, and the indulgent Pull Over Chocolate Cake were all top-notch, especially the chocolate cake, which was rich and gooey.

The service was attentive and prompt, complementing the excellent food. Overall, Flute Restaurant offers a well-rounded dining experience with great food, good service, and a pleasant setting. Definitely worth a visit if you're around Grant Road.

Had a heart-winning experience at All in 1 - Pure Jain Restaurant near Opera House, Charni Road, Mumbai!

Since I follow Swaminarayan traditions and rituals, this was a comfort place in all aspects.

The ambience was truly heartwarming, with attention to detail that made the space feel welcoming and vibrant. It was very informative to learn about jain practices and rituals w.r.t food as illustrated on their diverse menu.

I tried a few dishes and was genuinely impressed:
- Burmese Khowsuey: perfectly done with authentic flavors, all Jain-friendly!
- Schezwan Pot Rice: hard to find a pure Jain version in Mumbai, and this one had incredibly fresh, juicy veggies.
- Chimichanga: my first time trying it, and I absolutely loved the burst of Mexican flavors.
- Goti Soda: classic Gujarati twist, especially refreshing in raw mango and guava flavors.

The owner (Nirav Bhai) and manager were both very warm and welcoming, which added so much to the experience.

And just when I thought it couldn’t get better, they served a delightful mukhwas (mouth freshener) to wrap up the meal, a perfect finishing touch.

I also learned about their initiative of Jain Food Festival and their upcoming plans for opening a small supermarket for fresh & authentic ingredients.

My personal ratings are as follows:
Food: 9/10
Price: 9/10
Drinks: 8/10
Service: 10/10
Quantity: 11/10
Location: 10/10
Ambience: 10/10
Authenticity: 10/10
Insta-worthy: 10/10
Vegetarian-Jain: 100/10

Definitely looking forward to visiting again! 🌱💛

featured_reviews.name: Shirish Shenolikar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Review: Soam Restaurant, Mumbai

We stay in Chembur and our family visited Soam restaurant in SoBo for the first time and enjoyed a truly satisfying vegetarian dining experience.

We ordered a wide spread of dishes — panki, sev puri, dahi puri, dahi bhalla chaat, watana ghughra, sada dosa, aloo puri with potato subji, thepla with red potato subji, moong dal khichadi and kadhi. Each item was flavorful, well‑prepared, and appreciated by everyone at the table.

The service was prompt and courteous, making the meal smooth and enjoyable. The atmosphere was decent, not extraordinary, but comfortable enough for a relaxed family outing.

One point worth noting is the pricing. Compared to similar restaurants in the suburbs, Soam is on the higher side. Perhaps this is the premium for being a very popular SoBo (South Bombay) restaurant.

Overall, Soam impressed us with its authentic flavors and variety. It’s a place we would recommend to anyone looking for wholesome vegetarian food in South Mumbai, while keeping in mind the pricing.

featured_reviews.name: alok singh
featured_reviews.review_text:
Soam near Babulnath Chowpatty is a lovely place to enjoy authentic, homely Gujarati food in a calm and welcoming setting. I visited on a weekday and had a wonderful, relaxed experience without any rush.

We tried the Undhiyu, Jowar Roti, Puri, and Mango Lassi, and everything tasted fresh, balanced, and full of traditional flavours. The meal ended perfectly with a delicious Kulfi.

The service was warm and attentive, and the overall atmosphere made the visit even more enjoyable. A great spot for anyone who appreciates simple, soulful Indian vegetarian food.

featured_reviews.name: Patricia
featured_reviews.review_text: Went here on a weekday afternoon and the place was packed. I had to wait 30 mins to get a table for 2. The staff was polite and courteous. We tried the pankhi which was served steaming hot. It was soft and delicious but the quantity is less for the price. Next up we tried the farsan platter which had a few pieces of the palak samosa, dhokla and pattice. All them were so tasty and fresh. We also decided to try the Jowar pita pocket which was good but could do with less mayo. Overall it's good to try the gujarati dishes, though it is on the pricey side.

featured_reviews.name: Indradeep Roy
featured_reviews.review_text:
Valet parking is available. It’s a pure Veg restaurant and being a prolific meat eater I was reluctant to visit to begin with. However, when I stepped out of the restaurant I had eaten to my hearts content and was super happy. Thus, I think it’s worth everyone to visit and try out. The food was very different to the ones we are accustomed eating

I actually started with dessert and ordered a special of the day which was served on a milk base.

Then I ordered the Oondhiya. Normally it’s served with puri , but I requested only the sabzi and i relished it completely. I would surely recommend to try it.

We also had Gatte ka sabzi and Satpadi which was quite nice as well. It was served on dried loaves that was placed over plates. Innovative way to keep the plates cleaner and easy to wash.

I guess a visiting once again to try out a few more dishes in the future

featured_reviews.name: Jay Haria
featured_reviews.review_text: The mutter paratha with aloo-dahi sabzi was comfort food done well, balanced and not oily. The mutter pattice had a crisp exterior with a fresh filling, and the panki was soft and fragrant as expected. The guava drink added a refreshing, mildly sweet finish.

featured_reviews.name: Sumit K
featured_reviews.review_text:
Food is good and freshly made, no doubt about that. Taste is nice and feels authentic, but honestly the price is toooo high compared to the quantity 😕. Most dishes are around 400 per person and the portion is very less, only enough for one person. Feels a bit over hyped when you look at the quantity vs price.

That said, they do serve really good quality **authentic Gujarati food**. It’s a pure veg place with items like khichdi, ras puri, shrikhand, dal dhokli, bajra no rotlo, handvo, pooran poli, chaat and many more. They also have Jain food and fasting food during upvas, which is a plus. Taste is good, just wish the quantity was better for the price.

featured_reviews.name: anujoy bardhan
featured_reviews.review_text: Went here for a family dinner after visiting the iconic Khetwadi Ganpati. We had the special thali, which comes with 2 butter chapatis, papad, one paneer sabji, one mixed dal, one sweet, dal and rice. We also had shahi paneer with butter nan and butter chapatis. All of the above items were delicious 😋. We then ordered the dahi vada and that was good too. We had a toddler with us and he was allowed to eat his baby food which we had carried with us. The service was quick for the thaali ,dahi vada, nan and chapatis but the shahi paneer took slightly more time. The bill came around ₹798 for 3 adults, so roughly ₹266 per person , overall good value for money.

featured_reviews.review_text:
⭐⭐⭐☆☆

Mixed experience overall.

The best dish by far was the Paneer Butter Masala — rich, flavorful, and perfectly cooked. Easily 5/5. The Amritsari Chole with Paneer Kulcha was also quite good and satisfying, around 4/5.

The Paneer Tikka Masala Biryani was decent but nothing special, around 3/5.

What disappointed the most were the Malai Chaap and Afghani Chaap. Both felt quite bland and lacked proper flavor or seasoning. Definitely not worth the hype — around 2.5/5.

Good paneer gravy and chole kulcha, but the chaap needs major improvement.
